_doc: Secret-expansion registry (2026-09-18). THE EXTENSION POINT for secret_expansion_guard.py: adding a protected env var or credential store means editing THIS file plus one C-row in docs/specs/2026-09-18-secret-expansion-guard-shapes-spec.md, never the guard code. Mirrors data-plane-registry.json's contract: a missing or corrupt registry makes the guard PASS THROUGH with a WARN, because an infra failure must never brick Bash. Verbs are NOT here on purpose - they are shape semantics owned by spec section 4, not per-fleet data.
_secret_env_var_patterns_doc: Matched against the variable name with re.search, so anchor them. Deliberately suffix-anchored rather than substring: an unanchored TOKEN would catch TOKEN_BUDGET and similar, and superscar #3 says the cure for one leak must not be a guard that denies everyday commands. Printing anything ending in _API_KEY/_TOKEN/_SECRET/_PASSWORD is suspicious by definition, which is what makes the tight pattern safe here. The two vendor prefixes are listed whole because Builder Contract 3 names ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as a banned entity, not a spelling, and OPENAI_API_KEY is a live paid key on this fleet.
_secret_files_doc: PURE credential stores only - files whose entire purpose is holding secrets. Deliberately EXCLUDES ~/.qwen/settings.json, which is a config file that legitimate work must read and which PR #6765 emptied of credentials precisely so it would stop being a secret store; registering it would deny config work on migrated hosts to protect a file that no longer holds a secret. Known gap on unmigrated hosts (Pro still keeps the key there) - the cure is migrating Pro, not blocking config reads. Globs are matched against both the ~-expanded and the realpath-resolved candidate.
